key_insight: vdW confinement in confined epitaxy does more than steer adsorption and diffusion; it generates strong interfacial forces that mechanically couple to monolayer NbSe2 growth.
engineering_relevance: Engineering the interfacial mechanical landscape could improve high-throughput synthesis of high-quality 2D materials grown by confined epitaxy.
method: AI-assisted DFT calculations of monolayer NbSe2 growth between c-plane sapphire and h-BN
Computed force-electronic landscape at the interface to quantify atomic forces
Compared interfacial interaction energy with reported adsorption and diffusion energies
evidence_signal: The abstract reports large calculated forces of +0.070 and -0.04 eV/Å on Nb and Se and a unit-cell interfacial interaction energy up to 2.4 eV, indicating a strong mechanical contribution.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on computational modeling, so experimental validation is still needed before using interfacial mechanics as a design rule for growth.
paper_title: Resolving the interfacial mechanical landscape of monolayer NbSe2 grown by confined epitaxy
